name: Activity correlator — one estate's night, told as two stories and a gap
_why: The agent that is not about a cloud. Its evidence is the platform's own
record, so it needs no customer credential and reads the same whether the
estate is AWS, on-premises or both — which is the difference between a
catalog of vendor scripts and an agentic platform.
Four behaviours are pinned, and each is one that a model asked to
* eleven events become TWO stories, not eleven bullets;
* the automation that failed four times is separated out as standing
noise rather than being allowed to dominate the live incident;
* the approval sitting unactioned since 19:40 is surfaced — nobody
watches the inbox overnight, and 'we thought that had run' is a real
* proximity is reported as a SEQUENCE and explicitly not as a cause,
because this evidence cannot see the mechanism.

script.text: Eleven events, and they are two separate stories plus one thing nobody has actioned.

findings.summary: Three checks against app-prod-02 failed within four minutes of each other at 02:11–02:14, all with connection or timeout errors. That is one event, not three, and it is the only thing overnight that looks like a real incident.
Patch Deployment finished at 02:04, seven minutes before the first of those failures. That is a sequence worth checking and not a cause I can establish from this record.
Log Rotation failed four times on the hour with the same disk-quota error. That is a broken automation rather than part of the incident, and it has been failing all night.
An EBS volume cleanup has been sitting unapproved since 19:40 — over twelve hours — so anyone assuming it ran is wrong.

script.text:
**One real incident on app-prod-02 at 02:11, one automation that has been broken all night, and an approval nobody has actioned since 19:40 [e:1101].**

## The incident — app-prod-02, 02:11 to 02:14

Three checks failed within four minutes, all against the same host [e:1101]:

| Time | What | Error |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 02:11 | App Health Probe | connection refused on app-prod-02 [e:1101] |
| 02:12 | Queue Depth Check | connection refused on app-prod-02 [e:1101] |
| 02:14 | Synthetic Login | timeout after 30s [e:1101] |

That is one event. The host stopped answering and three things noticed in turn.

Worth checking first: Patch Deployment finished at 02:04, seven minutes before the first failure [e:1101]. That is a sequence, not a cause — this record shows what our automation did, not what patching changed on the host — but it is the obvious place to look, and whoever ran it will know in a minute whether that host was in scope.

Nothing has failed against app-prod-02 since 02:14, and the 06:00 Daily Health Report succeeded [e:1101]. It appears to have recovered on its own, which is worth saying out loud on the call because it means nobody fixed it.

## Standing noise — Log Rotation

Log Rotation failed four times, on the hour, every hour, with the same disk-quota error on /var [e:1101]. That is a broken automation rather than part of last night — it would have failed identically on a quiet night. Different problem, different person, and it should not be described as part of the incident.

## Waiting on a human

The AWS Unused EBS Volume Cleanup has been pending approval since 19:40, requested by s.iyer [e:1101]. Nobody watches the approvals inbox overnight. If anyone believes that cleanup has run, it has not.

## What this does not show

This is the record of what AutoOps did in this project. It does not show what an engineer did by hand, what changed in a cloud console, or what the customer's own monitoring saw — so if app-prod-02 was affected in ways nothing here probed, that will not appear above.

output_contains: That is a sequence, not a cause
